subject: Post-call: performance checkpoints & SLA questions (NebulaHealth)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@nebulahealth.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: performance checkpoints & SLA questions (NebulaHealth)

Hi Emma / Rajiv — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

What we heard:
- SLO targets: P95 latency target for interactive chat flows ~ < 300ms server-side; P99 requirement for peak/critical paths to be < 700ms. Streaming tail behavior is important for your clinician UX.
- Throughput & concurrency: initial peak forecast ~ 250 concurrent sessions, average sustained ~ 60 rps, with bursts to 500 rps during peak windows.
- Streaming: server-side stream chunking every 150-300ms preferred; client can handle partial updates.
- Reporting cadence: weekly latency/availability digest in early phases, rolling into monthly SLA reports after production cutover.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows, customer-backed traffic spikes (DDoS), and force majeure events.

Asks / open items for confirmation:
1) Do the latency targets above match the internal bar you need for clinician flows? If not, please state the p95/p99 numbers you require.
2) For measurement: do you prefer server-side completion time (Redwood-measured) or synthetic client-side RTTs? We recommended server-side for consistency.
3) Remedies: you mentioned interest in service credits + a joint remediation runbook. Are you ok with a tiered credit structure (sample attached)?
4) Any procurement constraints we should know about (PO timing, contract language around remedies)?

Next steps I propose:
- Vivek to share the measurement methodology doc (attached) and confirm how we measure streaming tail and concurrency.
- Redwood to send a draft SLO appendix with explicit measurement windows, exclusions, reporting cadence, and a sample remedies schedule (attached).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Vivek for Tuesday next week to validate telemetry integration.

Attachments: redwood-performance-playbook-draft.pdf, measurement-checklist.xlsx

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@nebulahealth.com>

Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance checkpoints & SLA questions (NebulaHealth)

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap, very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 < 300ms looks right for non-critical flows; for the primary clinician path we actually want p95 < 250ms if possible. P99 < 700ms is fine.
- Measurement: we prefer server-side metrics from Redwood for contract measurement. Can you confirm what the exact event is ("response_complete" vs "last_token_emitted")? We need this so our telemetry team can map it.
- Reporting: weekly during pilot is good; procurement would like to see the monthly SLA PDF included as an exhibit in the SOW.
- Remedies: procurement asked whether remedies can be capped per month vs per incident — they prefer a capped monthly credit.

I'll loop procurement on any legal/finance-level questions. Procurement: can you confirm PO lead times and if Nebula needs a redline window?

Happy to join the technical deep-dive — Rajiv will coordinate with Vivek on suitable times.

Emma
Director, Product Operations
NebulaHealth
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@nebulahealth.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance checkpoints & SLA questions (NebulaHealth)

Thanks, Emma — quick technical clarifications (see attached measurement-methodology.md):

1) Measurement event: Redwood will use server-side "response_complete" (time when last token is emitted by the serving runtime) for contractual latency. That excludes client-side network RTT. We also emit client-observed synthetic pings if you want to compare.
2) Streaming tail: we measure time-to-first-token (TTFT), inter-token spacing, and time-to-last-token; streaming SLOs are defined on inter-token 95th percentiles and the time-to-last-token p95/p99 as separate metrics.
3) Warm cache behavior: during cold starts we exclude the first N minutes per node (standard exclusion). We'll document the cold-start window and how it maps to autoscaling events.
4) Concurrency semantics: concurrency = number of active sessions with open KV cache + active stream. We'll provide a concurrency gauge and the histogram used for billing.
5) Measurement windows: we use a 5-minute sliding window for availability, and daily/weekly aggregates for reporting. The contractual measurement for latency percentiles will be computed over 30-day rolling windows to account for burstiness.

Attachment: measurement-methodology.md

If you want, I can add a short appendix showing synthetic vs server-side deltas from our pilot dataset. Happy to walk through the metrics on the technical call.

—Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance checkpoints & SLA questions (NebulaHealth)

Emma — appreciate the fast read. A couple of contract-level proposals from our side to reduce ambiguity and match expectations: 

1) Measurement definition: use Redwood server-side "response_complete" as Vivek outlined. We'll include a short examples appendix that maps the event to both streaming and non-streaming flows.
2) Remedies: propose a tiered monthly credit model (sample in attached playbook):
   - Single incident where monthly availability falls below 99.5% -> 5% monthly credit (capped at 25% of monthly fees)
   - Repeated or severe breaches escalate to 10% credit and remediation planning
   - Credit is calculated on monthly recurring fees only (not add-on usage).
3) Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (72h notice for non-critical), force majeure, customer-configured heavy traffic (bot flood) verified via telemetry, and third-party infra outages.
4) Reporting cadence: weekly during pilot, monthly SLA PDF after first 30 days in production.

We want to avoid per-request token-level exceptions in the core SOW; we can add a separate billing appendix to address usage accounting. If procurement needs a different credit cap or a per-incident model, we can negotiate but want that documented up front.

I'll be on the technical call to sign off on the measurement appendix. Tessa / Marissa — please include the SOW exhibit with the sample credits and measurement appendix in the next send.

—Sean
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
